order_design.type: cyclic Latin square, five cycles over 20 seeds
order_design.limitations: position balanced, not fully carryover balanced

measurement_window.origin: monolith application start (includes data/JVM initialization); distributed request after readiness; report this asymmetry and cold-start separately; no end-to-end latency equivalence claim

factor_changes: sequential versus parallel replacement evaluation inside one monolith Java process
distributed pipeline 1 versus 3 with fixed neighborhood parallelism 3 and IWSSR admission cap 3

hypotheses.status: Prespecified before v14 seed 199 technical pilot. New controls motivated by v13; no confirmatory reuse of v13 outcomes.
hypotheses.primary: Completed trained validation evaluations / 2700 s; exclude post-deadline completions and holdout. Two paired contrasts: monolith-n3 minus monolith; distributed-w1-n3 minus monolith-n3.
hypotheses.primary_test: Two-sided exact paired sign-flip tests over 20 seeds, Holm across two primary contrasts. Paired percentile bootstrap 95% CI, 20000 replicates, seed 20260926.
hypotheses.quality_guardrail: Individual one-sided 95% bootstrap lower bound, mean paired held-out macro-F1 difference, margin -0.005. Monolith-n3 vs monolith; each distributed vs monolith-n3. No simultaneous guarantee.
secondary_family: unique trained subsets and qualified distinct subsets
published quality-yield AUC, descriptive due to publication policy differences
CPU-hours and GiB-hours with coverage, CPU cost per trained evaluation
macro-F1, precision, recall, subset size, dimensionality reduction
late and rejected work, actual concurrency peak, initialization and end-to-end time
hypotheses.holdout_policy: Test once after validation selection. No tuning, exclusion or arm choice based on test performance.
hypotheses.technical_gate: All artifacts valid, actual parallel peak >1 and <=3 for monolith-n3, same classifier outputs on synthetic fixed subsets, ordered ties preserved, no late final selection, no surviving containers. Low quality is not failure.
limitations: Single host and frozen split, search seeds do not replicate datasets
Monolithic neighborhood parallelism does not overlap construction with local search
No pipeline-parallel monolith in this stage: distributed w3 contrast cannot isolate distribution from pipeline scheduling
Monolithic controller uses Python and embedded Java evaluator; distributed uses Spring/Kafka, with different overhead and component CPU partitions
Monolith initialization inside selection versus distributed service readiness outside selection is an explicit timing asymmetry
Publication events and Kafka consumer endpoints differ; no inference of lower client latency from these alone
New controls do not retroactively validate a universal architectural superiority claim

automatic_release.gate: Manual audit after technical pilot; no automatic formal release for v14
automatic_release.on_failure: Stop; no automatic retries and no selecting by holdout
